answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to lock a small, time-delayed stake before it can join a work thread. The stake acts like an ember: cheap to keep alive for an honest agent that keeps working, but costly to scatter across many fake identities, because each copy must fund its own stake and wait out the delay. New identities therefore cannot wander in, grab rewards, and vanish; they must first prove sustained, useful work in one thread, so creating a thousand sybils costs a thousand stakes and a thousand waits, while one real agent pays once.
